content.title: Route to Homes results with destination, valid dates, and guests preserved
content.intent: Prove the complete-input flow routes from the homepage to Homes results and preserves destination, dates, and guests in the results header.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow for homepage-to-results navigation; eqp for typed destination classes. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. No covering-array reduction was needed because the outcome stays the same and only destination type varies materially in-source; this scenario sweeps city and region as equivalent destination representatives.

content.title: Route to Homes results without dates and add dates from the results page
content.intent: Prove the partial-input flow routes with destination and guests only, preserves those inputs, and allows dates to be added later on the results page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow for homepage-to-results navigation; eqp for the explicit no-dates path and typed destination classes. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. The omitted-dates path is a source-defined supported variation, so it is modeled as its own scenario rather than a negative case.

content.title: Refine Homes results with Filters after homepage search
content.intent: Prove the results page exposes Filters and updates results after a filter is applied.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: pagination/search-list filtering profile for results refinement; state_flow because the path starts from routed search results. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. I kept this separate from Map because Filters-update behavior and Map-based refinement are different observable outcomes in the source.

content.title: Refine Homes results with the Map after homepage search
content.intent: Prove the results page exposes the Map and supports location-based refinement for the current search.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: pagination/search-list profile for collection refinement; state_flow because the path starts from routed search results. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. I kept this separate from Filters because the source gives Map its own refinement behavior.

content.title: Edit destination, dates, or guests from the results header
content.intent: Prove search parameters remain visible and editable on the results page so the guest can refresh results without returning to the homepage.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow for routed-results editing; eqp because destination, dates, and guests are equivalent editable parameter families named by the source. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. This is separate from initial routing because editability is a post-route behavior with its own oracle.

content.title: Navigate homepage search and results refinement controls by keyboard
content.intent: Prove the homepage search fields and CTA are reachable in order by Tab and the results-page Filters and Map controls are keyboard-accessible with visible focus indication.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: a11y for focus order and visible focus state; state_flow because the path spans homepage controls and results-page controls after routing. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. I kept homepage and results keyboard promises together because the source defines both as keyboard navigation requirements on the same web journey.

content.title: Keep English-IN labels for search fields and Search CTA on homepage and results
content.intent: Prove the journey keeps the labels Where, Check-in, Check-out, Who, and Search across the homepage and results pages.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: i18n for source-defined English-IN copy continuity; eqp because the same label set must hold on both homepage and results surfaces. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. This remains separate from routing because copy preservation is a localization promise, not a navigation outcome.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it proves the primary complete-input route and preserved context promised by the use-case.
[value_score] High value because the source explicitly calls the no-dates route a supported flow and it changes expected preserved inputs.
[value_score] Medium-high value because Filters availability and update behavior are explicit post-route refinement promises.
[value_score] Medium-high value because Map availability and map-based refinement are explicit post-route promises distinct from Filters.
[value_score] Medium value because editable search parameters prevent forced back-navigation and are explicitly stated in the source.
[value_score] Medium value because keyboard navigation is an explicit accessibility requirement affecting reachability of core controls.
[value_score] Medium-low value because copy continuity matters, but failures here are less blocking than broken routing or refinement.
